- tests/test_merge_lease.py:672-682 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: In `TickMetrics.test_grant_timestamp_is_taken_before_unlabel_and_dispatch`, the assertion `assertLessEqual(int(rows[1]["ts"]) - int(rows[0]["ts"]), 3, out)` requires the gap between the released and granted timestamps to be at most 3 seconds. The work before the grant (queue selection, jq filtering, PR-path lookup, lease write) has no time bound.
  WHY: On a loaded runner the work before the grant can take more than 3 seconds even when the grant timestamp is correctly captured before unlabel and dispatch (scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1685 vs :1687), so the test can flake. Both reviewers gave severity NIT, mapped here to low. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly declined to re-raise this item as a theoretical or already-accepted residual.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1634-1637 | severity=low | confidence=2

  PROBLEM: In `_mt_merge_lease_tick`, the `tick_waiters` jq spawn starts one extra `jq -s` process per lease ref per tick only to count waiters. It runs even when the holder path skips the metric block, because the `tick_metric_ok` check gates only the metric call.
  WHY: This adds N extra jq spawns per poll on the hot path. The reviewer says the overhead is negligible and not a real runtime defect, and reports it because the gate is in the wrong place. Source severity was NIT, mapped here to low.

- tests/test_merge_lease.py:TickMetrics.test_grant_timestamp_is_taken_before_unlabel_and_dispatch (line 682) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The assertion `assertLessEqual(int(rows[1]["ts"]) - int(rows[0]["ts"]), 3, out)` compares two whole-second `date -u +%s` readings across a busy pipeline that runs before dispatch and has no time bound: `tick_base_prs` jq filtering, `_merge_lease_queue_first`, the jq head lookup, `_merge_lease_pr_paths`, `_merge_lease_write` and a second `date -u +%s`.
  WHY: Under heavy load the work before dispatch can take more than 3 seconds while the timestamp is still correctly captured before the 5-second dispatch stub (scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1685 vs :1687). The 2-second margin is narrow enough to flake.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:_mt_merge_lease_tick, the `tick_waiters` jq spawn (around line 1634-1637) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: An extra `jq -s` process is spawned per lease ref per tick only to compute the waiters count. It runs even when the holder path skips the metric block, because `tick_metric_ok` gates only the metric call, not the `tick_waiters` jq.
  WHY: This sits on the hot path for every poll and costs N extra jq spawns for N lease refs. The cost is negligible in absolute terms and not a real runtime defect; it is reported as NIT because the helper gate is in the wrong place.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
